subject: Procurement readiness & commercial path — next steps (Acme)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme.com>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@acme.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Procurement readiness & commercial path — next steps (Acme)

Hi Samantha and Tom,

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and proposed next steps so procurement and engineering can align: 

1) Procurement path
- You mentioned AP prefers PO for purchases over $10k, and P-card is possible for lower-value pilots. Please confirm typical approval lead times and who we should loop into the PO process (billing contact + legal).
- Marketplace interest: you said that AWS Marketplace would help internal approvals, especially for security and procurement. Let us know if Marketplace listing is required up front or can follow the initial pilot.

2) Commercial preferences
- Pilot: suggested 90-day pilot to validate latency/cost with a scoped traffic pattern.
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private: we should scope a hosted (Redwood API) pilot first. If you need guaranteed throughput or data isolation, we can provide Dedicated capacity options and a Private deployment plan; we will include cost/commit tiers for each.

3) Pricing/commit options we will provide
- On-demand hosted rates (no commit)
- Monthly commit tiers for Hosted and Dedicated (examples: 0.5, 2, 5 TB token equivalent)
- One-time pilot discount and short-term commit for the pilot period

Next steps I suggest:
- I will send a pricing worksheet and draft SOW for pilot. (attached: Redwood_PRICING.xlsx, Acme_SOW_v1.pdf)
- Please share procurement contact and any PO templates or billing instructions.
- If Marketplace is required, confirm and we'll include marketplace pricing and timing implications.

Are you available for a quick 20-minute sync on Friday to confirm PO vs P-card and Marketplace yes/no?

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@acme.com>
Date: 2027-05-15T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Procurement readiness & commercial path — next steps (Acme)

On 2027-05-15 09:12, Marissa Cole wrote:
> Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and proposed next steps so procurement and engineering can align: 
> 
> 1) Procurement path
> - You mentioned AP prefers PO for purchases over $10k, and P-card is possible for lower-value pilots. Please confirm typical approval lead times and who we should loop into the PO process (billing contact + legal).

Thanks Marissa, this looks right. A few clarifications from our side:

- Procurement: our AP team prefers PO for anything > $10k. For pilots under that threshold we typically use a P-card. Lead time for POs is about 7-10 business days once legal signs off; faster if we can use a Marketplace procurement flow. Our billing contact is procure@acme.com and procurement lead is Michael Ortiz (michael.ortiz@acme.com).

- Marketplace: We are interested in AWS Marketplace listing for later stages, but for the initial pilot our legal team is fine with a direct SOW if it is standard. Marketplace would speed corporate purchasing but will add 2-3 weeks to onboarding if you need to complete seller onboarding first.

- Dedicated vs Hosted: For the pilot we prefer hosted to move quickly. If the pilot shows clear latency/throughput requirements, we'll evaluate Dedicated with a 6-12 month commit. Can you provide committed throughput tiers and monthly commit pricing for Dedicated? Also include any data isolation SOW language for Dedicated/Private.

- Attachments: please include a short SOW and billing instructions.

I'll book the Friday sync for 11am PT.

Thanks,
Samantha
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Corporation
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>

Subject: Fwd: Procurement readiness & commercial path — next steps (Acme)

Team,

Forwarding Acme thread — key asks from Samantha:
- Billing contact: procure@acme.com, procurement lead Michael Ortiz (PO lead).
- Pilot: hosted first, 90 days, likely < $25k for PO vs P-card threshold.
- Interested in Marketplace for later, but pilot can be direct SOW.

Can Aditya and Dev please prepare:
1) A pricing sheet with: hosted on-demand rates, hosted monthly commit tiers, Dedicated monthly commit tiers (0.5/2/5 equivalent tiers) and associated discounts.
2) A short SOW snippet for pilot and a Dedicated/Private data isolation paragraph for legal.
3) A recommended pilot offer (90 days) with a one-time onboarding credit and a trial commit (if any) to get procurement comfortable.

Lauren, please join the Friday sync and be ready to confirm commercial positioning (pilot vs proof) and suggested deal guardrails (cap on spend, exit terms).

I'll attach the current pricing workbook and SOW to the calendar invite.

Thanks,
Marissa
Enterprise AE

Marissa — thanks for coordinating. Quick update from procurement:

- We can issue a PO for the 90-day pilot. Expected value is under $25k and should fit within standard approval. I'll have Michael Ortiz send PO instructions to procure@acme.com. Attached is our internal PO instructions PDF.

- Marketplace: we would like to evaluate AWS Marketplace but not required for pilot. If Redwood can provide a Marketplace listing later, that would be ideal for corporate procurement.

- Billing: procure@acme.com is the billing contact. Please send an updated SOW that references hosted pilot, 90 days, expected throughput target of 50 qps peak, and scoping for Dedicated if performance requires it.

DocuSign for the SOW would be preferred. Here's a placeholder link for routing once you post the new SOW: https://www.docusign.com/prepare/abc123
